roleContext.jobDescription: The card payments change team at a mid-sized retail bank delivers the changes that the card schemes and the bank's processor make mandatory: token lifecycle updates, authentication rule changes and revisions to settlement files. The project manager keeps the integrated plan and RAID log, books certification test windows with the processor and the schemes, writes the steering-committee report and takes change requests through the change advisory board. For mandated changes the project manager is expected to own delivery, including the scope decisions and the go/no-go call, and to account for those decisions to the steering committee.

candidate.originalCvMarkdown:
# Curriculum vitae

Target role: Project Manager, Card Payments Change

## Experience

- Project analyst, then project manager, at Kestrel Card Services from June 2021 to February 2024; kept the integrated plan and RAID log for the 2023 token-lifecycle change, going through risks and dependencies each week with the four workstream leads.
- Booked the processor and scheme certification test windows, circulated the test calendar to the workstreams and logged the defects the processor raised against each test cycle.
- Deputised for the programme director on the token-lifecycle change, preparing the scope-change papers that the programme director put to the steering committee for decision.
- Wrote the fortnightly steering-committee status report: milestones, RAG status, the top five risks and the decisions requested from the committee.
- Raised change requests for the card-processing platform through the bank's change advisory board, attaching an impact assessment and a back-out plan to each submission.

## Work samples

- Work sample: a portfolio page titled 'What my colleagues said' that accompanies the candidate's token-lifecycle case study. It quotes three colleagues: 'the real owner of the token-lifecycle change from start to finish', 'made every call that mattered' and 'true ownership, all the way through'. The page carries the quotations and the colleagues' first names only.
